title: On-Prem Control Plane: Conversation Guide for Risk, Legal & Procurement
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a pragmatic conversation guide for sales and solutions engineers when engaging Risk, Legal, and Procurement stakeholders about Redwood's on-prem / VPC control plane options for regulated workloads. Focus: decision criteria, concrete mitigations, and short contract language to accelerate procurement cycles.

Audience notes:
- Risk / InfoSec: wants clear boundaries on telemetry, remote access, patch/update model, and breach impact.
- Legal / Compliance: asks about data processing, data residency, breach notification, and auditability.
- Procurement: cares about liability caps, SLAs, change control, and onboarding timelines.

One-line positioning to open with:
"Redwood’s optional private control plane lets you keep critical operational control and auditing on your network while still receiving managed orchestration — we split operational telemetry from customer data and give your team explicit controls over access and updates."

Key distinctions (simple language):
- Control plane types we offer:
  - Fully self-hosted control plane (Customer-managed): customer runs all control plane services in their VPC/on-prem. Redwood provides installer + upgrade artifacts and support SLA. No outbound telemetry unless customer enables it.
  - Hybrid control plane (Private control plane with minimal managed agent): control plane control APIs run in customer environment; a small, optional agent can call Redwood endpoints for non-sensitive telemetry (opt-in).
  - Hosted control plane (Redwood-managed): standard hosted control plane with RBAC and VPC peering options — suitable when regulatory constraints are lighter.

Common buyer objections and suggested responses (concise):
- Objection: "If you run the control plane, you could access our keys or data."
  - Response: "For our private and self-hosted options, the control plane is deployed inside your network and we do not have direct access. We ship non-privileged operator tooling; secrets are injected via your KMS/HSM and never leave your environment. We can include explicit isolation language in the contract."

- Objection: "How do we get timely security patches if the control plane is self-hosted?"
  - Response: "We provide signed update bundles, automated patch tooling for orchestration, and a 30/60/90 escalation policy. For high-risk CVEs we offer a hotfix channel and emergency deployment checklist. We also provide a managed fallback policy for emergency remote patching with pre-approved runbooks and auditable logs if you choose that option."

- Objection: "What telemetry do you collect and could it be used to reconstruct PII?"
  - Response: "Telemetry is intentionally minimal: health metrics, agent heartbeats, and anonymized performance counters. For private/self-hosted installs we default to zero-telemetry; any telemetry is opt-in and documented. We can sign specific telemetry allowances in the DPA and provide a telemetry whitelist in the SOW."

- Objection: "We require proof of no exfiltration/persistent remote access."
  - Response: "We provide: deployment manifests, signed installer checksums, a forensic-ready logging mode, and a vendor access policy that enumerates emergency support steps. We will include contractual commitments to notify and provide a forensic package if remote access is used."

Contract and procurement-ready snippets (copy/paste friendly):
- Data custody line: "Customer retains sole ownership and custody of all Customer Data. Redwood shall not access Customer Data except as explicitly permitted in this Agreement or as required to provide agreed-upon managed services with Customer authorization."

- Telemetry clause: "Redwood shall collect no production data payloads from Customer systems under the private control plane deployment. Telemetry, if enabled, will be limited to anonymized operational metrics and agreed log categories. Any telemetry collection will be disclosed in writing and is subject to Customer approval."

- Emergency access & notice: "In the event Redwood must perform an emergency action that requires remote access or change to Customer systems, Redwood will: (a) obtain written pre-authorization per the approved runbook, or (b) in life/safety or regulatory scenarios, provide notification within 48 hours and a full activity log within 7 days."

- SLA & liability highlights: "SLA metrics for Dedicated/Private installs are adjustable; standard offer: 99.9% platform orchestration availability for control plane APIs. Liability caps exclude willful misconduct; where required we can adjust limitations to comply with customer procurement rules in exchange for a higher commitment tier."

Risk matrix (quick):
- Risk: Unauthorized vendor access -> Mitigation: private deployment, no vendor keys, HSM integrations, runbooked emergency access.
- Risk: Slow vulnerability response -> Mitigation: signed hotfixes, emergency channels, optional managed patching add-on.
- Risk: Audit evidence missing -> Mitigation: forensic-ready logs, SIEM integration (Syslog/OTLP), retention options.
- Risk: Regulatory data residency -> Mitigation: control plane and data plane can be colocated in customer region; we mirror artifacts for DR in your region only via customer-approved channels.

Technical clarifications to have ready:
- Keys/Secrets: We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, or on-prem HSM). Private deploy: operator credentials never leave KMS.
- Updates: Installer is signed; upgrades run as orchestration jobs inside customer VPC. Optionally, an airgap bundle can be delivered for classified environments.
- Logs/Telemetry: Provide list of log types by default and for optional telemetry. Include example Syslog/OTLP endpoints and retention configs.

Competitive notes (how to frame it vs. common alternatives):
- Against fully-managed cloud providers: emphasize local control, zero-exfil guarantee options, and the ability to place control plane inside regulated networks.
- Against pure self-hosted open-source runtimes: Redwood provides hardened installers, signed updates, and an SLA + emergency support channel; we own the orchestration code and offer optional managed services to reduce time-to-production.
- Against vendors that insist on persistent connections: highlight our runbooked, auditable, and opt-in remote access model.

Customer decision checklist (what procurement/risk will ask for):
- Deployment diagram showing network flows and ingress/egress rules.
- List of data categories and confirmation that payloads never leave customer environment.
- Access policy and pre-authorized runbook for emergency actions.
- Signed DPA and SOC2 report (or equivalent) + evidence of patching policy.
- Installer digest/signature and airgap bundle option.

Sales/Solutions engineer quick script (5–7 minutes for initial stakeholder call):
1) Intro / intent (30s): "We're focused on minimizing exposure while giving you predictable operations for LLM inference: keep keys and data under your control, choose who can access the control plane, and get a maintainable upgrade path."
2) Confirm constraints (1–2 min): "Can you confirm: must control plane run inside your network? Any constraints on outbound connections? Required certifications (e.g., FedRAMP, ISO)?"
3) Walk the model (2 min): show the three deployment options and recommended starting point for regulated workloads (private control plane with opt-in telemetry or fully self-hosted if required).
4) Risk mitigations (1 min): list keys/patching/auditability features and that we can add contract language.
5) Next steps (30s): SOW draft, low-risk PoC (airgap bundle + test harness), security questionnaire handoff.

Red team / security evaluation checklist (for technical reviewers):
- Verify installer signature and validation procedure.
- Confirm KMS/HSM integration and verify private key never exported.
- Review network ACLs and ensure no outbound flows except allowed endpoints.
- Request a sample of logs and verify PII redaction rules.

Open negotiation levers (what we can offer without product changes):
- Extended onboarding support hours and remote runbook walk-throughs.
- Higher SLA tier for orchestration availability.
- Short-term telemetry-free pilot with explicit audit handover.
- Insurance/back-to-back indemnity adjustments for certain enterprise customers.

Appendix: suggested artifacts to attach to customer packet:
- Deployment diagram template (editable).
- Sample DPA excerpt with telemetry and data custody language.
- Installer signature verification guide.
- Emergency runbook template and escalation contacts.

Notes for internal reviewers:
- This doc is intended to be used by AE + SE pairs — personalize examples for regulated verticals (healthcare/finance/government).
- Flag any customer asking for live remote maintenance without a pre-approved runbook — that is a security red flag and requires Legal review.

Version history:
- 2025-11-12: initial draft (Maya)

Open questions (to resolve before final):
- Define exact telemetry whitelist for private control plane (owner: Product Privacy)
- Decide standard SLA numbers for self-hosted installs (owner: SRE/Product)
- Create a formal airgap-distribution checklist for classified pilots (owner: Release Eng)

Action items:
- SEs: add this guide to your playbook and share feedback after three customer calls.
- Legal: review suggested contract snippets and return redlines.
- Product: confirm telemetry whitelist and update release notes for airgap artifacts.
